Published online:
September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
Global (primary: US, Asia-Pacific, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — recap of overnight/Tuesday events
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Fed meeting Sept 16, bond rout trajectory, inflation anxiety
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
US airstrikes on Iran have triggered a risk-off cascade across global markets. Oil (Brent ~$95.45) is at a five-week high on Strait of Hormuz disruption fears, driving a broad bond selloff — US 10Y yield hit 4.8122%, near a three-year high; Japan 10Y at 3.015%, a three-decade high. Asian equities sold off sharply (KOSPI -4%, Nikkei -2.9%), with S&P 500 futures modestly lower (-0.1%) after Wall Street's prior session decline (SPX -0.7%, Nasdaq -1%). Fed rate hike odds at the Sept 16 meeting jumped to 67% (from ~40% a week ago). RBNZ hiked 25bps but struck a dovish tone, pressuring NZD. USD firmed. Gold, BTC, and ETH all dipped modestly.

---

**Q01.** Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US stock market pricing?
Relevance: **YES** — Directly covers US 10Y yields, Fed rate hike probability, S&P 500/Nasdaq performance, USD, and geopolitical drivers (Iran strikes) affecting all of the above.

**Q02.** Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: **72/100** — The US-Iran military escalation is a materially new geopolitical shock. The bond selloff and inflation re-ignition risk it creates are unexpected developments layered on top of an already hawkish Fed backdrop. The jump in Fed hike odds (39.6% → 67%) in one week signals rapidly shifting market consensus, adding uncertainty.

**Q03.** Is the content explicitly about bullish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: **NO**
Impact score: **5/100** — No bullish narrative present. Only marginal positive would be USD strength, which is itself a risk-off signal.

**Q04.** Is the content explicitly about bearish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: **YES**
Impact score: **72/100** — Multiple converging bearish vectors: surging yields crowding out equities, oil shock reigniting inflation fears, rising probability of an additional Fed hike, and active geopolitical risk (Strait of Hormuz). S&P futures already pointing lower. Analysts explicitly warn of a "volatile month ahead."
